usage: This is the most common way to say congratulations in Egypt, used for weddings, graduations, new jobs, or buying a new car. It is suitable for all formalities and relationships. While 'mabrouk' alone is also used, adding 'alf' (a thousand) makes it warmer and more standard.

variants.label: casual/short
variants.note: Use this for smaller achievements or in very casual passing.

variants.label: very enthusiastic
variants.note: Use this to show extreme excitement, often for close friends' weddings or major life events.

variants.label: to a groom
variants.note: Use this specifically to congratulate a male friend or relative on his wedding day.

responses.english: May God bless you (to a man)
May God bless you (to a woman)
May the same happen to you (to a man)

examples.transliteration: alf mabrouk 3ala el shoghl el gedeed.

examples.arabic: أَلْف مَبْرُوك يَا حَبِيبِي، رَفَعْت رَاسْنَا.
examples.english: Congratulations my dear, you made us proud.
